title: Coq au Vin
subtitle: Chicken braised in red wine with mushrooms and lardons
excerpt: Chicken pieces browned and braised in a full bottle of red wine with lardons, button mushrooms, shallots, and thyme until deeply flavoured and tender. The sauce reduces to a glossy, wine-dark coating.

recipe.sourceNotes: Coq au vin is a French peasant dish originally made with an old rooster (coq) that was too tough to roast and needed long braising in wine to tenderise. The modern version uses a jointed chicken, which cooks more quickly, and a full bottle of good red wine — typically Burgundy, Beaujolais, or Rhone. Like boeuf bourguignon, it was popularised in Britain and America through Julia Child's cookbooks. The dish benefits from being made a day ahead: the flavours deepen overnight, and the fat can be skimmed from the cold surface.

content.text: Brown the chicken pieces skin-side down and do not move them: this renders the fat from the skin and creates a deep golden crust. The wine reduces significantly during braising and becomes the sauce, so use one that you would be happy to drink. The dish is done when the chicken is pulling away from the bone.

items.preparation: bone-in, skin-on; or a whole chicken jointed into 8 pieces

content.text: Heat the oil in a large casserole over high heat. Season the chicken. Brown skin-side down for 6 to 8 minutes until golden, then turn and brown the other side for 3 minutes. Remove and set aside.
Reduce to medium. Fry the lardons until golden. Add the shallots and cook for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute.
Return the chicken. Pour in the wine and stock. Add the thyme and bay leaves. Bring to a simmer. Cover and cook over the lowest heat for 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes until the chicken is very tender.

In the last 15 minutes, fry the mushrooms in a separate pan in a little oil until golden. Stir into the casserole. Remove the thyme and bay leaves. Check seasoning. Scatter with parsley and serve with crusty bread or mashed potato.
